title: India On Track to Hit $1 Trillion in Exports This Year, Commerce Secretary Says
excerpt: Rajesh Agrawal's assessment at a FICCI session rests on record October data — $89.99 billion in total exports and a record $49.47 billion in goods — against last fiscal's all-time high of $863 billion.
body:
• Commerce Secretary Rajesh Agrawal said on Wednesday, November 18, that India is on track to hit the $1 trillion exports target for goods and services in 2026-27, speaking at a session organised by the industry chamber FICCI, PTI reported.
  • The target is a government projection, not a result: last fiscal year, India's exports touched an all-time high of $863 billion, Agrawal said.
  • The reported data behind the claim: total exports in April-October 2026-27 are estimated at $568.84 billion, up 16.66% from a year earlier, and October alone set records — $89.99 billion in total exports, up 29.9%, with goods exports at a record $49.47 billion, up 45.06%.
  • For diaspora investors and businesses, the caveats matter as much as the headline: the October services figures are estimates that may be revised, and the goods trade deficit widened to $39.88 billion in October, its highest in a year.

India is on track to hit its $1 trillion exports target for goods and services this financial year, Commerce Secretary Rajesh Agrawal said on Wednesday, even as he framed the country's advantage in uncertain global trade conditions as its standing as a "trusted" trading partner.

"We are on track to hit $1 trillion exports [of goods and services] this year," Mr. Agrawal said at a session organised by the industry chamber FICCI in New Delhi, PTI reported. He said the country's exports recorded a 16.6% increase in April-September this fiscal, and that last fiscal year India had touched an all-time high of $863 billion in exports.

"We are on track to hit $1 trillion exports [of goods and services] this year."

— Rajesh Agrawal, Commerce Secretary, at a FICCI session

What the reported data shows

The secretary's confidence rests on the trade figures the Commerce Ministry released on November 13. Total exports of goods and services in October rose 29.9% year-on-year to $89.99 billion — the highest monthly export value India has ever recorded, up from $69.27 billion in October 2025, according to the ministry's quick estimates. Goods exports alone hit an all-time monthly peak of $49.47 billion, a 45.06% jump from $34.11 billion a year earlier and the fastest monthly merchandise growth in five years, Agrawal told a virtual media briefing while releasing the data.

Cumulatively, total exports during April-October 2026-27 reached an estimated $568.84 billion, up 16.66% from $487.59 billion in the same period last year. The October record was driven by petroleum products, electronic goods, engineering products, gems and jewellery, and chemicals. The growth was broad-based across markets: the Federation of Indian Export Organisations said shipments expanded to 43 of India's top 50 export destinations in October, with exports to the United States growing 39%, to China 48% and to Japan 45%.

The caveats in the same data

Two qualifications sit inside the record month. First, the services component — estimated at $40.51 billion for October, up from $35.17 billion a year earlier — is an estimate: the ministry cautioned that the latest actual services data from the Reserve Bank of India relates to September, and the October figures may be revised. Second, imports rose sharply too. The overall trade deficit narrowed to $20.09 billion in October from $25.15 billion a year earlier, but the goods deficit alone climbed to $39.88 billion, its highest level in a year, according to a Reuters calculation based on the government data. Cumulatively, the trade deficit for April-October widened to $93.35 billion from $83.25 billion.

K. Rangarajan, Vice-Chancellor of the Indian Institute of Foreign Trade, noted that a weaker rupee, higher petroleum exports and a favourable base effect also contributed to October's surge. He said the growth was driven largely by non-oil shipments, particularly electronic goods and mobile phones.

What to watch next

The $1 trillion figure remains a target the government has set for the financial year ending March 31, 2027 — Agrawal's statement is an assessment that the current pace reaches it, not a reported outcome. The next monthly trade releases will show whether October's record goods performance carries into November, and whether the services estimates survive revision when the RBI publishes actual figures.
